Aisha — thanks for the clear list. We've gone through the spreadsheet and sketched a reference diagram that follows your preferences for a split control/data plane and minimizes customer egress surface. Action items and what we'll deliver by EOD Monday: 

1) One-page reference diagram (PNG) showing: control-plane endpoints (Redwood control plane in our managed VPC), customer-managed data-plane nodes (in StratusHealth VPC), transit/peering boundaries, allowed egress destinations, and recommended NAT/bastion placement.

2) Acceptance checklist (PDF): topology items + integration checklist (KMS thumbprint exchange, required firewall rules, BGP session params if chosen).

3) Ops runbook (short): day-0 cutover steps, rollback triggers, and egress validation test plan.

Quick notes for your team:
- We're proposing a dedicated VPC peering with explicit route tables per tenant subnets; we can also support a single-transit VPC with policy-based filters if you prefer central egress.
- For certificate management, Redwood will support issuing service certs signed by your KMS-backed CA via an automated rotation job; we need your KMS admin to provide a service principal for the initial handshake.
- If you prefer BGP for dynamic failover, we will publish ASN and suggested prefixes; otherwise our recommended initial approach is static routes with a scheduled failover test.

Attachment: redwood_splitplane_reference_v1.drawio.png (PNG, 240 KB)

Proposed time for a quick sync: Mon Jun 17 14:00 PT — 30 minutes to walk the diagram and sign off on the acceptance list. Does that work for your team?

Thanks — Mateo

On Fri, Jun 15, 2028 at 10:14 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com> wrote:
> Aisha — thanks for the clear list. We've gone through the spreadsheet and sketched a reference diagram ...

Adding a few technical clarifications from the runtime/infra side: 

- Egress: we'll offer two hardened egress patterns. Pattern A (recommended): customer-controlled egress via a managed NAT gateway in their VPC; Redwood will accept a restricted set of destination CIDR blocks and TLS SNI filters. Pattern B: Redwood-proxied egress where token-level auditing is enforced; this increases latency and cost, but centralizes logging for compliance. 
- BGP: if Stratus wants BGP, we'll peer using private ASN 64512/64513 and expect you to advertise tenant prefixes. We will provide a BFD session to speed detection of failures.
- Certificate rotation: Redwood supports Vault-backed issuing (HashiCorp Vault) or direct KMS sigs; for GovCloud we recommend direct KMS sign to avoid cross-region replication issues. We'll need the KMS key ARN and a rotation window (30/60 days).

I've uploaded the initial egress validation checklist to the shared drive (link below) and included a minimal test plan as an attachment we can run in staging once connectivity is confirmed.

Attachment: egress_test_plan.md (text, 6 KB)
